1.headline: Caleb Williams drops 41 in a 59-37 track meet, and Mike opens the season with the league's top score.
1.dek: The highest-scoring Week 1 in NFL history, three-touchdown Sundays for King Henry and Swift, and one league team that forgot to show up. Week 1 is in the books.

paragraphs: If you had Bears–Panthers going 59–37 on your bingo card, congratulations, you are a liar. Caleb Williams put up 334 total yards and four touchdowns, D'Andre Swift scored three times, and the two teams combined for the highest-scoring Week 1 game the NFL has ever played. Sunday's slate as a whole averaged a record 53.3 points a game, which is great news if you started skill players and terrible news if you started a defense.

Elsewhere the ground game did the heavy lifting. Derrick Henry ran in three scores for Baltimore, Jahmyr Gibbs went for 186 yards and two touchdowns, and Bijan Robinson piled up 173 yards on the way to a 35-point fantasy day. Josh Allen threw four touchdowns and engineered a 96-yard drive to win it late, which is a very Josh Allen thing to do. Rookie Jaxson Dart threw three touchdowns to beat Dallas on Sunday night, and Tyler Shough threw for 410 yards in New Orleans and still lost 31–30 in overtime to Detroit, because of course he did.

Now the bad news. Ja'Marr Chase caught two passes for 12 yards. Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Colston Loveland (zero catches) were all invisible. Matthew Stafford and the Rams managed 7 points in Australia against the 49ers, and Christian McCaffrey got 32 touches without doing much with them. The injury report is already ugly: A.J. Brown's ankle is expected to cost him around six weeks, Brock Bowers is out with a knee injury, Zay Flowers went for 150 yards before pulling a hamstring, Isiah Pacheco landed on IR, and Kyler Murray left Sunday's game in Green Bay, handing the Vikings' offense to Carson Wentz.

bullets.label: Biggest blowout
bullets.text: Raiders 27, Dolphins 13, with Ashton Jeanty running for 147 yards and two touchdowns. Cardinals over Chargers 26–14 was the upset of the weekend, and the 49ers held the Rams to 7 in Australia.

bullets.label: Closest call
bullets.text: Lions 31, Saints 30 in overtime. Eagles 24, Commanders 22 and Seahawks 13, Patriots 10 in the Wednesday opener were the other one-score sweats.

bullets.label: Breakouts
bullets.text: Keon Coleman went 8 for 112 and a score, Hollywood Brown saw 16 targets, and Caleb Williams looked like the QB1 everybody kept saying he could be.

bullets.label: Duds
bullets.text: Chase (2–12), London, Pitts, Loveland, Stafford. Joe Burrow also looked out of sorts, which rarely lasts, but ask Shane how Week 1 felt.

bullets.label: Injuries to watch
bullets.text: A.J. Brown (ankle, ~6 weeks), Brock Bowers (knee), Zay Flowers (hamstring), Isiah Pacheco (IR), Kyler Murray (left game). Patrick Mahomes returned from his ACL and looked fine, thanks for asking.

games.2026-w1-3: Mike's Washington C-Words posted the week's high score, and did it the hard way: with Caleb Williams dropping 41.26 for the other side and the Chargers D/ST contributing a clean zero. David Montgomery (27.4), Zay Flowers (23.5) and a 21.7-point Dallas Goedert game carried the day. Ethan got the QB of the week and still lost by 28, thanks mostly to Ja'Marr Chase (2.2) and George Kittle (2.2) combining for fewer points than his kicker.
games.2026-w1-2: The rookie is real. Jaxson Dart threw for 32.6 in his Sunday night win over Dallas and Nick's receivers (St. Brown 23.7, Olave 23.2, Moore 18.5) did the rest in a 137.4-point opener. Shane actually got the two best running back games in the matchup, with D'Andre Swift (31.9) and Ashton Jeanty (29.7), but Burrow's 16.16 and a combined 9.1 points from Pickens, Harrison Jr. and his kicker left Slim Pickens 15 short. Shane also left 60.2 points on the bench, which will sting.
games.2026-w1-5: Nate opened as a slight underdog and won by 26. Trevor Lawrence (34.1) and Kenneth Walker III (32.6, on 13.3 projected) out-scored their projections by 33 points between them, and even Tyler Loop the kicker chipped in 14. Johnny got Jalen Hurts (30.72) and Justin Jefferson (27.2) and nothing else: his other seven starters combined for 48.2. Not the Week 1 the GOAT was hoping for.
games.2026-w1-0: Josh Allen's four-touchdown comeback was worth 39.66 to Chase, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chuba Hubbard added 22.2 apiece in a comfortable 31-point win. Smalls had the single best non-QB game of the week in Derrick Henry (34.8, three touchdowns) and it barely mattered: Drake Maye (11.82), Saquon Barkley (8.5), a 2-point kicker and a 1-point Rams D/ST sank T Smalls to 101.02.
games.2026-w1-1: The closest game of the week, and one Caleb was projected to win by 8.5 anyway. Jahmyr Gibbs (31.1) and Javonte Williams (21.7) did the work while Justin Herbert (15.26) and a goose egg from Kyle Pitts kept it interesting. Drew's Lamar Jackson (26.96) and Jonathan Taylor (23.6) were great, but Courtland Sutton and Jake Ferguson combined for 3.7, and Off In Church came up 9.2 short.
games.2026-w1-4: Kevin's God Hates Jags scored 104.6, which would have lost to eight of the other ten teams this week, and won by 56. Conor's The Love Doctor put up 48.6: Stafford 4.1, A.J. Brown 4.1, Loveland 0, and a Browns D/ST that finished at minus one. Bijan Robinson (27.3) and Trey McBride (20.0) were all Kevin needed. For context, that is the fourth-lowest regular-season score by anyone in this league since 2019, out of 1,164.

awards.playerOfWeek: Three rushing touchdowns and 34.8 points for the 32-year-old who was supposed to be slowing down. It came in a loss, which is very on-brand for a Smalls team.
awards.qbOfWeek: 334 total yards, four touchdowns and 41.26 fantasy points in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. Ethan started him, and Ethan lost by 28. Fantasy football is a cruel game.
awards.dud: Projected for 21.65, delivered 4.1 as the Rams scored a single touchdown in Australia. He was one of six Love Doctor starters under 4.2 points, so the blame is shared, but he's the one wearing the badge.
awards.differenceMaker: Projected for 13.3, scored 32.6, and Nate won by 26 in a game he was projected to lose. Take Walker's surplus away and this one is a coin flip.

1.predictorNote: First-week projections lean heavily on ESPN's rest-of-season lineup values and each owner's era-adjusted history, so one big Sunday moves the needle less than you'd think. It'll trust the actual results more every week from here.

2.headline: Chase drops 155 behind Josh Allen's five touchdowns, and the Bears go from 59 points to three.
2.dek: Four teams are 2-0, the Panthers defense outscored Lamar Jackson, and the closest game of the week came down to a point and a half.

paragraphs: Last week the Bears scored 59. This week they scored 3, in the wind and rain against Brian Flores' Vikings defense, and the 56-point drop is the largest by any team since 1973. Caleb Williams was carted off with a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter (imaging was clean, and he hasn't been ruled out for Week 3), Colston Loveland caught one pass for three yards, and Rome Odunze and Luther Burden combined for 75 yards. Anybody who started Bears players had a bad Sunday, which in this league is a lot of people.

The good news came Thursday and Sunday night. Josh Allen opened the new Highmark Stadium with three passing touchdowns and two rushing scores in a 41–31 shootout with Detroit, where Jared Goff (327 yards, four touchdowns) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (9 for 142 and two scores) put up numbers in a loss. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 155 yards and three touchdowns from Drew Lock, including an 82-yarder. Dak Prescott went 26 of 31 with four touchdowns and passed Tony Romo as the Cowboys' all-time leader, with CeeDee Lamb going for 153 and two. Davante Adams had 195 yards and two scores on Monday night with Puka Nacua out, Matthew Stafford threw four touchdowns, and Patrick Mahomes threw for 382 in an overtime win over the Colts in which Travis Kelce topped 100 yards for the first time since 2024.

Now the bad. Jaxson Dart hurt his knee on the Giants' opening drive and gave way to Jameis Winston. Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow again, the same injury that wrecked his 2025. DJ Moore left Thursday's game with a shoulder, Jayden Reed was carted off with a neck injury, Dallas Goedert hurt a knee, Saquon Barkley had a stinger, Nico Collins is out about two weeks with a hamstring, and Brock Bowers isn't expected back until Week 4. Ashton Jeanty managed 44 yards on 14 touches, Bijan Robinson had 81 total yards against a Carolina defense that gave up 59 points a week ago, Justin Jefferson caught three passes, and Justin Herbert fumbled three times and threw two picks to a fifth-round rookie.

bullets.label: Biggest blowouts
bullets.text: Panthers 34, Falcons 3, a week after Carolina allowed 59. Bryce Young threw for 287 and three scores and Devin Lloyd had two picks, a sack and a pick-six. Seahawks 31–7, 49ers 35–13, Rams 28–6 and Patriots 20–3 rounded out the routs.

bullets.label: Closest calls
bullets.text: Eagles 24, Titans 20 on a last-second Jalen Hurts drive. Packers 20, Jets 17 in overtime, the first team in the Super Bowl era to win with under 200 yards, 10-plus penalties and no turnovers. Chiefs 33, Colts 30 in overtime. Browns 23, Buccaneers 19.

bullets.label: Breakouts
bullets.text: Smith-Njigba's hat trick. Dalton Schultz went 12 for 140 on 14 targets in Houston. Jalen Coker caught eight passes. TreVeyon Henderson ran for 76 and a score in his debut, and Kenneth Walker III has 175-plus scrimmage yards in both games, the first player to do that since 1980.

bullets.label: Duds
bullets.text: The entire Bears offense. Jeanty (44 yards), Bijan (81 total yards), Jefferson (3 for 55), Herbert (five giveaways), Brian Thomas Jr. (4 for 49 on 12 targets) and Courtland Sutton (1 for 6).

bullets.label: Injuries to watch
bullets.text: Caleb Williams (hamstring), Jaxson Dart (knee), Jayden Daniels (elbow), DJ Moore (shoulder), Jayden Reed (neck), Dallas Goedert (knee), Nico Collins (hamstring, ~2 weeks), Brock Bowers (knee, back around Week 4).

games.2026-w2-7: Chase's 155.12 is the high score of the season so far, and his 287.28 points through two weeks is the fourth-best start by anyone in this league since 2019. Josh Allen (46.82) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (38.0) combined for 84.82, which by itself would have beaten two full teams this week, and Christian McCaffrey added 20.6. Shane got a 37.78 from Jared Goff and still lost by 56.74: his other eight starters combined for 60.6, and Slim Pickens is 0-2 despite scoring the most points of any winless team.
games.2026-w2-9: Dak Prescott (37.76, four touchdowns and the Cowboys' record) and Davante Adams (35.5 on a 195-yard Monday night) carried Kevin to 2-0 while Bijan Robinson managed 9.6. Nick actually put up a respectable 114.4 with Jaxson Dart (0.8) hurt on the Giants' first drive and DJ Moore (-0.1) done after one quarter on Thursday. Amon-Ra St. Brown's 30.7 and a 16-point Brandon Aubrey kept it interesting, but two zeroes at QB and flex is too much to overcome.
games.2026-w2-8: The Panthers defense scored 24 for Drew on four takeaways and a Devin Lloyd pick-six, Jonathan Taylor went for 27.2 in a game the Colts lost in overtime, and Jake Ferguson chipped in 18.3 while Lamar Jackson (16.8) had a quiet day in Baltimore's loss. Mike got 66.3 from Patrick Mahomes and CeeDee Lamb and 46.2 from everyone else: David Montgomery scored 3.4, and Dallas Goedert left with a knee injury at 0.9. Off In Church evens up at 1-1.
games.2026-w2-10: Ethan won by 29 with his quarterback carted off. Caleb Williams scored 7.72 before his hamstring gave out, but Ja'Marr Chase (23.0, two scores including the toe-tap catch of the year), DeVonta Smith (22.7) and George Kittle (16.0, 600th career catch) had it covered. Johnny's 82.06 was the week's low score, and the injury report explains a lot of it: Brock Bowers is out with a knee, Jordan Mason is on IR, Jonathon Brooks is doubtful, Jayden Reed (0.9) was carted off with a neck injury, Malik Nabers (0.6) is questionable after losing his quarterback on the first drive, and Kyler Murray got hurt in Week 1. Dalton Schultz (20.0) and Harrison Butker's game-winning night (16.0) were the whole show. Johnny Football Club is 0-2 for the first time since 2022. Most of Johnny's team has died. RIP.
games.2026-w2-11: Kenneth Walker III (20.8) and James Cook (20.4) did the work for Nate, whose 2-0 start is his first since 2022. The worry: Jayden Daniels scored 16.74 and then dislocated his elbow, so Loop There It Is needs a quarterback. Conor got a 34.98 from Matthew Stafford, a week after a 4.1, and his other eight starters totaled 53.2, with Colston Loveland (0.8) still stuck on 0.8 points for the season. There is a glimmer of hope, though. Next week's opponent is Ethan, whose quarterback Caleb Williams left Sunday on a cart with a hamstring injury and may not play. Stafford just threw four touchdowns, Kyren Williams has scored in double digits both weeks, and Puka Nacua's return would give The Love Doctor its best receiver back. And Conor has been here before: he started 0-2 in 2023 and still made the playoffs.
games.2026-w2-6: Two teams projected for a combined 224 scored 168, and Caleb survived by a point and a half. Justin Herbert (9.88, three fumbles and two picks) and Rhamondre Stevenson (3.1) nearly sank Chef Cale, but Jahmyr Gibbs (20.3) and a 19-point Dalton Kincaid fill-in got him to 2-0. Smalls got Saquon Barkley (2.5) knocked out with a stinger, a 1-point kicker and 5.0 from a banged-up Ladd McConkey, and T Smalls is 0-2 with two losses by a combined 32.6.

awards.playerOfWeek: Nine catches, 155 yards, three touchdowns and an 82-yard bomb, all from Drew Lock. Chase drafted him, started him, and is 2-0 because of him. Fifth receiver ever with 8-plus catches, 120-plus yards and a score in each of the first two games.
awards.qbOfWeek: Three passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and 46.82 points to open the new stadium in Buffalo. Allen and Smith-Njigba scored 84.82 between them, more than Johnny's or Smalls' entire lineups.
awards.dud: Last week's Sunday night hero took a hit to the knee on the Giants' opening drive and finished with 0.8 points against a 20.79 projection. Nick lost by 20, so Dart alone didn't decide it, but it certainly didn't help.
awards.differenceMaker: 195 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night with Puka Nacua sidelined, 22.4 points over projection. Kevin won by 20.06. Take away Adams' surplus and God Hates Jags loses to Nick.

2.predictorNote: Chase's 2-0, 287-point start moved him to the top, Caleb slid three spots after an 84-point win, and Drew is the week's big riser at four spots. The model now gives this season's results about a quarter of the weight, with ESPN's rest-of-season projections and career history covering the rest.
